newsitem.title: FRANCE: Grasp of philosophy essential for French students.
newsitem.headline: Grasp of philosophy essential for French students.

text.p: Can the course of history be altered? Does science preclude any form of religious belief?
These were among the questions launching this year's Baccalaureat exam on Monday, with nearly 630,000 candidates seeking France's coveted high school diploma.
The Bac, as it is universally known, is a requirement for university admission.
Other questions included: Is respect owed only to the individual? Is there a contradiction between the imaginary and the real? Does truth constrain or liberate?
Most students taking the examination are 17-18. The youngest was 14 and the oldest 77. The Bac was created under Napoleon to ensure equal opportunities for all to attend university.
